newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl to delay candidacy decision - party sources.
newsitem.headline: Kohl to delay candidacy decision - party sources.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl will not yield to pressure from within his party to announce soon whether he wants to stand in the 1998 election, top sources in his ruling Christian Democrats (CDU) said on Thursday.
The sources, who declined to be named, said it would not help Kohl or his party if he made an announcement in the next few weeks.
"That would not solve a single current problem," one Kohl aide told Reuters.

Disagreement within Kohl's coalition over major tax and pensions reforms intended to win it next year's election, as well as a sense of helplessness over runaway unemployment, have added to speculation that Kohl, 66, may not see out his term.
A report in the daily Die Welt on Tuesday said Kohl's allies in the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) were pressing him to make a decision, preferably to stay on, within the next eight weeks.

But the source said Kohl's behaviour and comments on the question of whether he would stand again suggested that the chancellor would only make a statement on the issue when he had shown some success in central policy areas.

On Sunday, Europe's longest serving head of governmment told French television he had not yet made up his mind but would ponder whether to stay on after June's European Union reform summit in Amsterdam.
By June, planned reforms to the tax and pensions systems could be agreed, providing a better background for Kohl to announce his candidacy, one source said.
He added that Kohl knew that his candidacy for the 1998 elections could be risky for himself, and would not guarantee for a CDU victory.
Commenting on a report in Thursday's Sueddeutsche Zeitung that Kohl wanted to be asked by his party to stand, the source said the party was already calling him.
He said Kohl would not stand again if the party was not behind him.
